study.title: Taxes on Generations over Time Periods
study.question: Using Real Dollars and Normalizing for Population Distribution, how much has the Tax Burden and Tax Rewards (in terms of how much benefits have been recieved from taxes by age group) fell on each generation? Track how different taxes have varied over the years too, I want plots of that AS WELL AS the other plots you WERE ALREADY GOING TO GENERATE, like sales tax, income tax, property tax, taxes on alcohol, gas, etc and factor in how much those affect different generations during different time periods factoring in stuff even as minute as average commute times (I want data and visuals for how different generations have different average commutes) affecting the carbon tax, vape tax targetting younger generations, property taxes impacting older generations. Everything.
study.dataset: Statistics Canada Distributions of Household Economic Accounts (DHEA, Tables 36-10-0587-01 & 36-10-0588-01), Survey of Household Spending by Age of Reference Person (SHS, Table 11-10-0227-01), Census of Population & Labour Force Survey Commuting Reference Tables (Tables 98-10-0458-01 & 98-10-0463-01), Canadian Tobacco and Nicotine Survey (CTNS 2022–2024, Table 13-10-0906-01), Canadian Institute for Health Information National Health Expenditure Database (CIHI NHEX 1975–2025), Office of the Parliamentary Budget Officer (PBO) Distributional Carbon Pricing & Fiscal Sustainability Reports, U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Expenditure Survey (BLS CEX), FRED CPI Deflator Series (`CPIAUCSL` / StatCan `v41690973`), and Auerbach-Gokhale-Kotlikoff Generational Accounting Benchmark Tables.

ST-09.summary:
To evaluate how fiscal burdens and rewards distribute across demographic cohorts over time, we construct a population-normalized, inflation-adjusted Generational Accounting panel in constant 2024 Canadian dollars ($\text{2024 CAD}$) spanning 1985 to 2025. Integrating Statistics Canada’s Distributions of Household Economic Accounts (DHEA) and Social Transfers in Kind (STiK) with CIHI age-specific expenditure curves, we define the real per-capita Net Fiscal Incidence ($\text{NFI}_{g,t}$) for generation $g$ in period $t$ as total direct and indirect taxes paid minus cash transfers and in-kind public services received, normalized by the cohort's population weight $P_{g,t} / P_t$:
$$\text{NFI}_{g,t} = \frac{1}{P_{g,t} \cdot \pi_t} \left[ \sum_{k \in \mathcal{K}} \tau_{k,g,t} B_{k,g,t} - \left( \text{Cash}_{g,t} + \text{STiK}^{\text{Health}}_{g,t} + \text{STiK}^{\text{Educ}}_{g,t} \right) \right], \quad \Gamma_{g,t} = \frac{\text{Rewards}_{g,t}}{\text{Taxes}_{g,t}}$$
where $\pi_t = \text{CPI}_t / \text{CPI}_{2024}$ is the price deflator, $\tau_{k,g,t}$ is the effective tax rate on tax base $B_{k,g,t}$ across instrument set $\mathcal{K} = \{\text{income, sales, property, fuel/carbon, alcohol, vape}\}$, and $\Gamma_{g,t}$ is the Fiscal Reward-to-Tax Ratio. Empirically, prime-working-age Generations X (ages 45–60) and Millennials (ages 29–44) carry the heaviest gross real per-capita tax

analytics.chartTitle: Real Per-Capita Tax Burden vs. Fiscal Rewards by Generation (2024 CAD)
analytics.chartSubtitle: Population-normalized annual total taxes paid (primary) vs. public cash + health/education transfers received (secondary) per capita across cohorts and historical life-cycle baselines (StatCan DHEA, SHS & CIHI, Constant 2024 $).

kpis.label: Peak Tax-Bearing Cohort (Gen X)
kpis.definition: Population-normalized real annual total tax burden (income, payroll, GST/HST, property, fuel/carbon, and excise) per capita for Generation X (ages 45–60) in constant 2024 dollars.

kpis.label: Senior Fiscal Reward Ratio (65+)
kpis.definition: Ratio of total real per-capita public benefits received (OAS/GIS, CPP/QPP, and CIHI age-weighted healthcare Social Transfers in Kind) to total direct and indirect taxes paid by cohorts aged 65 and older.

kpis.label: Commute Fuel & Carbon Burden Peak
kpis.note: Millennials (30–44) peak one-way commute & gross fuel/CO2 tax
kpis.definition: Mean one-way commute duration and resulting annual per-capita road-fuel excise plus carbon levy expenditure for Millennial commuters, driven by an 81.6% private vehicle modal share from exurban housing.

kpis.label: Gen Z Vaping Excise Share
kpis.definition: Share of total national federal and provincial vaping excise duty paid by Generation Z (ages 15–28), normalized for cohort population distribution and CTNS 30-day usage prevalence.

analytics.inspectorTitle: Generational Fiscal Incidence & Behavioral Micro-Model Inspector

inspectorParams.label: Aging Fiscal Shift Coefficient (β_65+)
inspectorParams.definition: Panel OLS fixed-effects estimate of the additional real annual net tax burden imposed on prime working-age adults (25–54) per 1 percentage-point increase in the 65+ population share.

inspectorParams.label: Commute-to-Carbon Tax Elasticity (γ)
inspectorParams.definition: Elasticity of gross household fuel and carbon tax expenditure with respect to cohort mean one-way commute duration, instrumented by metropolitan housing price-to-income distance gradients.

inspectorParams.label: Vaping Excise Age Concentration (CI)
inspectorParams.definition: Age-ranked concentration index of federal/provincial vaping excise duty payments across adult cohorts; negative values below -0.45 indicate severe concentration on cohorts under age 30.

inspectorParams.label: Senior Healthcare STiK Multiplier
inspectorParams.definition: Ratio of CIHI per-capita public healthcare expenditure for seniors aged 65+ ($14,042) and 80+ ($24,800) relative to the working-age baseline of $3,818/capita for ages 15–64.

inspectorAttrs.label: Prime-Age Income & Payroll Tax Concentration
inspectorAttrs.definition: Percentage of aggregate national personal income tax and CPP/EI payroll contributions funded by Millennials and Generation X (ages 29–60) after normalizing for population share.

inspectorAttrs.label: Exurban Auto Commute Exposure (Ages 30–54)
inspectorAttrs.definition: Weighted share of employed Millennials and Gen X commuting via private car, truck, or van across Canadian CMAs, driving peak gross fuel and carbon tax incidence.

inspectorAttrs.label: Boomer Homeownership & Property Tax Share
inspectorAttrs.definition: Homeownership rate among Baby Boomer households, resulting in the highest gross per-capita municipal property tax outflow ($2,640/capita) alongside the lowest effective tax-to-home-equity ratio.

inspectorAttrs.label: Cohort Fiscal Life-Cycle Asymmetry Index
inspectorAttrs.definition: Composite structural score measuring the expansion of the working-age net fiscal deficit between the 1990 Boomer baseline (ages 26–44) and the 2025 Millennial baseline (ages 29–44).

study.title: Automotive Recall Comparison
study.question: How to the total amount of recalls compare between different automotive companies, the severity of each recall should be part of a stacked column chart. Total cost and total customer loss from each.
study.dataset: USDOT / NHTSA Safety Recalls Flat Files & Annual Reports (49 CFR Part 573, DataHub mu99-t4jn, 2024–2025), Transport Canada Motor Vehicle Safety Recalls Database (MVSA SOR/2024-274), SEC Form 10-K / IFRS Warranty Reserve & Accrual Filings (Warranty Week 2025–2026 Benchmarks), JD Power U.S. Automotive Brand Loyalty Study (2025) & Reynolds Retention and Defection Report (2026), and Liu & Shankar (2015, Management Science) Recall Severity & Brand Preference Elasticity Benchmarks.

analytics.chartTitle: 2025 NHTSA Automotive Recalls by Severity Tier (Campaign Count)
analytics.chartSubtitle: Stacked comparison of High-Severity Physical/Mechanical Defect Recalls (Primary) vs. Low/Moderate-Severity Software & Compliance Recalls (Secondary) across top 10 OEMs (NHTSA Part 573, 2025).

kpis.label: Highest Recall Volume (2025)
kpis.definition: Total NHTSA Part 573 safety recall campaigns filed between Jan 1 and Dec 31, 2025. Ford accounted for 98 high-severity physical campaigns and 55 software/compliance campaigns.

kpis.label: Peak OEM Warranty Burden
kpis.definition: Total annual GAAP warranty and recall reserve addition, summing current-year vehicle accruals ($6.70B) and retroactive changes of estimate for pre-existing recall liabilities ($2.30B).

kpis.label: OTA vs. Physical Unit Cost
kpis.definition: Average per-vehicle recall remediation expenditure comparing Over-the-Air (OTA) firmware reflashing ($66.50/unit) against physical dealership service bay part replacement ($500 to $4,200/unit).

kpis.label: Industry Brand Retention
kpis.definition: Percentage of trade-in or lease-return households repurchasing the same automotive nameplate (JD Power 2025 / Reynolds 2026), where 1% loyalty loss equals ~$100M+ in lost OEM operating profit.

inspectorParams.label: Physical Severity Elasticity (β₁)
inspectorParams.definition: Estimated brand retention percentage-point reduction per unit log-increase in high-severity mechanical/propulsion/fire recall campaigns.

inspectorParams.label: Statutory Remedy Threshold (T*)
inspectorParams.definition: Federal regulatory window under 49 CFR 577.5 requiring OEMs to provide final recall remedy availability before issuing mandatory interim 'unrepaired defect' owner notices.

inspectorParams.label: 2025 U.S. Recall Fleet Scale (N)
inspectorParams.definition: Total U.S. motor vehicles impacted across 997 NHTSA recall campaigns in calendar year 2025 (alongside 72.7M total on-road vehicles carrying at least one open recall).

inspectorParams.label: Mean Lengthy Remedy Lag (T_lag)
inspectorParams.definition: Average elapsed calendar days between NHTSA Part 573 defect filing and final mailed owner remedy notification across complex hardware recalls (ranging from 98 days at Honda to 291 at Mercedes).

inspectorAttrs.label: OTA Software Remedy Capability (Tesla)
inspectorAttrs.definition: Share of total safety recall campaigns resolved remotely via Over-the-Air software updates without requiring a physical dealership visit.

inspectorAttrs.label: Mainstream Brand Retention Leader (Toyota)
inspectorAttrs.definition: Share of returning vehicle owners who repurchase the same brand in the 2025–2026 JD Power and Reynolds retention benchmarks (62.6%).

inspectorAttrs.label: North American Recall Completion Rate
inspectorAttrs.definition: Estimated proportion of recalled vehicles on U.S. and Canadian roads that successfully complete remediation within 36 months, leaving ~20–25% of on-road vehicles with open recalls.

inspectorAttrs.label: Prior-Year Reserve Adjustment Ratio (GM)
inspectorAttrs.definition: Share of total 2025 warranty reserve additions ($3.25B of $8.35B at GM) driven by retroactive upward 'changes of estimate' for older recalls such as the L87 V8 and Bolt battery.
